svg.aria-label: The Nefertiti figure with each of the 30 scored items removed in turn
svg.font-family: Gentium Plus, Source Serif 4, Georgia, serif
svg.text: What removing each piece of evidence does to the Nefertiti figure
Each bar runs from the figure with every item counted (89%) to the figure with that one item left out.
to the left: the item supports the identification
to the right: the item weighs against it

g.title: E01. Feminine grammatical forms attached to the extended-prenomen titulary. Without this item the Nefertiti figure is 84.6% (with every item 88.8%).
g.text: E01 Feminine endings on the throne name

g.title: E02. The nomen Neferneferuaten is Nefertiti's own cartouche name (Neferneferuaten-Nefertiti from about year 5), written with the same reversed Aten group. Without this item the Nefertiti figure is 76.0% (with every item 88.8%).
g.text: E02 Neferneferuaten is Nefertiti's own name

g.title: E03. Epithets tying the ruler to Akhenaten as his beloved and to a husband: mery-Waenre, mery-Neferkheperure, akhet-en-hies 'effective for her husband'. Without this item the Nefertiti figure is 81.7% (with every item 88.8%).
g.text: E03 Epithets tying her to Akhenaten and to a husband

g.title: E04. Stela UC 410 + Cairo JE 64959: the double cartouche of Neferneferuaten is cut over Nefertiti's single queenly cartouche and a king's-daughter caption. Without this item the Nefertiti figure is 84.9% (with every item 88.8%).
g.text: E04 Double cartouche on stela UC 410

g.title: E05. Paired-ruler scenes: an adult woman in the blue crown beside a male king, both with uraeus, interacting as living rulers; the Hermopolis pillar join names Neferneferuaten and King's Daughter Ankhesenpaaten. Without this item the Nefertiti figure is 86.2% (with every item 88.8%).
g.text: E05 Paired-ruler scenes: a woman in the blue crown

g.title: E06. Box Carter 1k: Akhenaten 'great in his lifetime', then Ankhkheperure-mery-Neferkheperure Neferneferuaten-mery-Waenre, then King's Great Wife Meritaten 'may she live', as three entries in one protocol. Without this item the Nefertiti figure is 69.1% (with every item 88.8%).
g.text: E06 Box Carter 1k: three names in one protocol

g.title: E07. Tomb of Meryre II (Amarna tomb 2) and the Memphis block: King Ankhkheperure Smenkhkare Djeserkheperu with King's Great Wife Meritaten, under the Aten, in a tomb whose dated decoration ends with the year-12 durbar. Without this item the Nefertiti figure is 88.5% (with every item 88.8%).
g.text: E07 Meryre II's tomb: Smenkhkare with Meritaten

g.title: E08. Calcite jar Carter 405: Akhenaten's cartouches followed by Smenkhkare's, both later erased; the only object joining the two names. Without this item the Nefertiti figure is 89.0% (with every item 88.8%).
g.text: E08 Jar Carter 405: Akhenaten's names with Smenkhkare's

g.title: E09. Complementary distribution of the names: the plain prenomen only with the nomen Smenkhkare, the extended prenomen only with the nomen Neferneferuaten, with no crossed example among hundreds of bezels and moulds. Without this item the Nefertiti figure is 88.6% (with every item 88.8%).
g.text: E09 Plain throne name only with Smenkhkare

g.title: E10. Pairi graffito TT 139: 'Year 3, III Akhet 10' of Ankhkheperure-mery-[...] Neferneferuaten-mery-[...], with Amun worshipped and a 'House of Ankhkheperure in Thebes' staffed by priests of Amun; Smenkhkare is otherwise attested only in Aten contexts. Without this item the Nefertiti figure is 88.7% (with every item 88.8%).
g.text: E10 Pairi graffito: her year 3 in a temple of Amun

g.title: E11. Amarna jar dockets: Akhenaten's highest year 17; a year-17 docket relabelled 'year 1' (COA III 279); years 1-3 of a successor at Amarna; 'House of Smenkhkare, [justified]' in a year 1 (no. 35); 'House of Ankhkheperure' as a separate estate (no. 36). Without this item the Nefertiti figure is 88.8% (with every item 88.8%).
g.text: E11 Amarna jar dockets: years 1 to 3 after year 17

g.title: E12. Manetho according to Josephus: Orus, then 'his daughter Akencheres, 12 years 1 month', then 'her brother Rathotis, 9 years'. Without this item the Nefertiti figure is 91.6% (with every item 88.8%).
g.text: E12 Manetho: "his daughter Akencheres"

g.title: E13. A shabti of Nefertiti with queenly titles only (Louvre AF 9904 + Brooklyn 33.51). Without this item the Nefertiti figure is 93.0% (with every item 88.8%).
g.text: E13 Nefertiti's shabti with queenly titles only

g.title: E14. Masculine references beside the extended names: 'my lord' with a masculine article on Ranefer's door jamb; the North Riverside Palace prenomen painted with r, not t, under mer. Without this item the Nefertiti figure is 88.9% (with every item 88.8%).
g.text: E14 Masculine references beside her names

g.title: E15. Age of Neferneferuaten-tasherit: fourth daughter, shown as a child at the year-12 durbar, so at most about ten years old in year 17. Without this item the Nefertiti figure is 86.1% (with every item 88.8%).
g.text: E15 Age of the daughter Neferneferuaten-tasherit

g.title: E16. Dayr Abu Hinnis graffito: Nefertiti still King's Great Wife on day 15 of a month of Akhet in year 16, about a year before Akhenaten's death. Without this item the Nefertiti figure is 89.9% (with every item 88.8%).
g.text: E16 Dayr Abu Hinnis: Nefertiti still queen in year 16

g.title: E17. A full kingly burial outfit made for the female king was left unused and re-inscribed for Tutankhamun (coffinettes, pectoral, trappings, middle coffin, mask, second shrine, statuettes). Without this item the Nefertiti figure is 88.8% (with every item 88.8%).
g.text: E17 Her burial outfit reused for Tutankhamun

g.title: E18. Two rulers with one prenomen: Ankhkheperure is shared by the Smenkhkare name-set and the Neferneferuaten name-set, which has no parallel for two successive kings. Without this item the Nefertiti figure is 89.0% (with every item 88.8%).
g.text: E18 Two rulers sharing one throne name

g.title: K01. Age at death of the KV55 body: six hands-on examiners give 19-26; Harris and Wente 30-35 and Hawass 2010 (CT, criteria unpublished) 35-45; Akhenaten had a daughter by about year 2 and reigned 17 years. Without this item the Nefertiti figure is 89.1% (with every item 88.8%).
g.text: K01 Age at death of the KV55 body

g.title: K02. Inscribed material in KV55: magic bricks of Akhenaten, Kiya's coffin re-worked with Akhenaten's epithets (cartouches later cut out), Kiya's canopic jars, Tiye's shrine, sealings of Tutankhamun; no name of Smenkhkare. Without this item the Nefertiti figure is 88.8% (with every item 88.8%).
g.text: K02 Inscriptions in KV55

g.title: K03. 2010 STR pedigree (8 loci): KV55 a son of Amenhotep III and KV35EL (Tiye) and the father of Tutankhamun with KV35YL; no independent replication; Gad et al. 2020 same team. Without this item the Nefertiti figure is 88.8% (with every item 88.8%).
g.text: K03 The 2010 DNA pedigree

g.title: K04. Tutankhaten was 'King's Son of his body' at Amarna; if the pedigree holds, his father is the KV55 man, who must therefore have been a king. Without this item the Nefertiti figure is 89.0% (with every item 88.8%).
g.text: K04 Tutankhaten as "King's Son"

g.title: D01. The name: Ni-ip-hu-ru-ri-ia-as (KBo 14.12 iv 18) against Nebkheperure (Tutankhamun) and Neferkheperure (Akhenaten); EA 9 addressed to Nibhurrereya. Without this item the Nefertiti figure is 88.4% (with every item 88.8%).
g.text: D01 The name Nibhururiya

g.title: D02. The Armaa synchronism: Horemheb acts in Syria as a non-king in years 7-9 of Mursili II (KUB 19.15 + KBo 50.24), which sits badly with a Nibhururiya who died only four years before Horemheb's accession. Without this item the Nefertiti figure is 88.9% (with every item 88.8%).
g.text: D02 The Armaa synchronism

g.title: D03. Season: the death message reached Suppiluliuma during the Carchemish campaign (late summer or autumn) and Hani came back in spring; Tutankhamun's burial flowers point to a death in winter; Akhenaten died after the year-17 vintage. Without this item the Nefertiti figure is 88.8% (with every item 88.8%).
g.text: D03 Season of the king's death

g.title: D04. The widow's plea: 'my husband died, a son I have not, I will never take a servant of mine and make him my husband'; Ankhesenamun was later paired with Ay on a ring; Nefertiti and Meritaten each had daughters and a boy in the family. Without this item the Nefertiti figure is 88.8% (with every item 88.8%).
g.text: D04 The widow's plea

g.title: D05. Lupakki's raid on Amka at the time of the king's death (Deeds) matches EA 170 from the Amarna archive, and the envoy Hani of the Deeds appears in EA 161, 162 and 369. Without this item the Nefertiti figure is 88.8% (with every item 88.8%).
g.text: D05 Lupakki's raid on Amka

g.title: D06. Hittite relative chronology: the plague prayers, the 20-year plague, and the solar omen of Mursili's year 10 (eclipse of 24 June 1312 if that is the omen). Without this item the Nefertiti figure is 88.8% (with every item 88.8%).
g.text: D06 Hittite relative chronology

g.title: D07. Consistency of the plea with the Egyptian succession: a widow writes that Egypt has no king; a coregent already on the throne, or an Egyptian king who acceded after months of negotiation for a Hittite prince, fit that less well. Without this item the Nefertiti figure is 88.7% (with every item 88.8%).
g.text: D07 The plea against the Egyptian succession

g.title: D08. 'A son he has not' against Tutankhaten's existence: if the dead king was Tutankhaten's father, the statement is false for the royal house. Without this item the Nefertiti figure is 89.0% (with every item 88.8%).
g.text: D08 "A son he has not"
